target_customer: Consumers learning to speak a foreign language, starting with Korean English learners, plus workplace plans from 2024
problem: Language apps teach vocabulary but give little speaking practice, and human tutors are expensive.
business_model: Consumer subscription, monthly or annual, with a free trial

founders.name: Connor Zwick
founders.background_notes: YC page states the Flashcards+ sale to Chegg. TechCrunch 2024 says the founders met at the Thiel Fellowship.

founders.name: Andrew Hsu
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as cofounder and CTO.

technical_complexity.rationale: Speech recognition and conversational feedback for learners were hard in 2017, and the product matured only with later AI models.

defensibility.rationale: Learner speech data and a content method help, but large incumbents can add similar AI tutoring.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Duolingo added generative AI features and TechCrunch 2024 still compares Speak mainly to Duolingo. No source found on a purchase.

market_need_then: Learners in markets such as South Korea spend heavily on English speaking practice. The founders launched in Korea in 2019 per TechCrunch 2024.

branding.domain_note: Uses speak.com, an exact match .com; how it was acquired is not stated in sources I found.

brand_strength.rationale: A one-word exact .com name tied to the core action, with large user growth reported, but no source on brand assets or community.

outcome_analysis: Speak entered YC in Winter 2017 and built a speaking-first tutor, launching in South Korea in 2019, then raised a 27 million dollar Series B in November 2022 led by the OpenAI Startup Fund. Later extensions reached a reported 500 million dollar valuation in June 2024 with over 10 million users. Growth was helped by the generative AI shift and a focused first market.
notes: Series C of $78M at $1B valuation led by Accel in Dec 2024 appears only in a search snippet from Multiples.vc and is unverified, so it is not recorded as a round. TechCrunch 2024 gives total raised about $84M, above the $63M in the recorded rounds, so earlier seed and Series A rounds are missing. The Series B-2 label is from search snippets of speak.com; amount and date come from TechCrunch's headline listing. Competitor search found only current lists and no 2017-dated sources, so the list is empty. TechCrunch says launched in 2014 in one place, the founding year 2016 comes from Speak's own blog. Name origin search found nothing.
